newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica govt urges mines to preserve rural economy.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica govt urges mines to preserve rural economy.

text.p: The downscaling of the labour force in the mining industry should not take place at the expense of the mostly rural areas that have traditionally been recruitment areas, a new government policy paper said.
Released on Tuesday, the paper was commissioned by the Labour Ministry in the wake of major moves to cut costs in the gold mining industry as more mines became marginal.
"Currently, the social costs of downscaling are in effect being displaced on to the economies of the countryside," the paper said.
In the medium term, ways should be investigated in which infrastructure and resources from mining could be transferred to local economies after downscaling.
All this called for the gradual downscaling of mines, "adequate" retrenchment packages and the diversification of rural economies to create jobs and growth.
At the same time, the labour market should be restructured to establish a more stabilised workforce while recognising the broader dependence on mining wages in some areas.

Particular attention would have to be paid to the position of miners from neighbouring countries through a revision of agreements on their working conditions and an investigation into welfare provisions for them, the report said.
The report said wages in the mining industry were below the poverty line and wage revisions should be accompanied by revised grading, the removal of racial hierarchies and better skills training.
"New standards need to set to ensure that accidents and diseases associated with mining are no longer seen as inevitable consequences of the nature of the work," the report said.
